number: 0004
title: Plan for English-first display and default stemmed/substring search
status: draft
date: 2026-10-24
feature: english-first-substring-search
inputs: [.specs/architect/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0030-english-stemming-index-for-default-search.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0031-quoted-terms-are-exact-matches.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0032-english-first-display-with-original-underneath.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0033-unquoted-terms-match-stem-or-substring.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0034-english-stem-index-as-expression-index.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0035-stemming-scope-and-summaries-searchable.md, .specs/search/0003-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/data/dba/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/telemetry/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/ux/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/testing/backend/0004-english-first-substring-search.md]
principles: [P1, P3, P5, P7, P8]
supersedes: null
---

# 0004 Plan for English-first display and default stemmed/substring search

## 1. Summary
Build two changes on the shipped translation feature: (1) English-first headlines and text with the original underneath, and (2) default search that matches English word forms and partial words, with quotes for exact matches and summaries made searchable. Two phases, about 22 to 31 hours in total. Critical path: migration (four concurrent indexes) → compiler → list query → plan tests → UI. The database and query work (phase 1) must land before the UI (phase 2) can show matched sides and English excerpts.

## 2. Inputs
All specs and ADRs in the front matter, present and read. Skipped by choice: carma-devops (nothing new to run; the migration-at-start-up concern is a task here) and carma-data-sanity (ILIKE escaping and escaped rendering are covered in test tasks). Mode: sequential. Specs were amended in place (still drafts) after the late decisions in ADR-0035; they were not re-run.

## 3. Blockers and open questions
No blockers. Open items to track (all have a safe default):
| # | Item | Owner | Default if unanswered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | Summary language: assumed English | Human, check 20 real summaries in phase 1 | English |
| Q2 | Wording of the "no summary yet" coverage line | Human | Wording in UX 0004 section 5.5 |
| Q3 | "Machine translated" tag on every translated card | Human | Every card |
| Q4 | `pg_trgm` enabled in the target database | Human, T1.2 | Flag `trgm_index` decides at runtime |
| Q5 | Index size and write cost at 800/s | Human, after B1 | Extrapolation only, labelled |
| Q6 | Keep legacy beacon values one release | Human | Keep |

## 4. Consistency report
| # | Finding | Class | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Architect 0004 sections 1 and 5.3 say "no migration expected"; ADR-0030/0034/0035 require migration 0007 | Note | Decisions recorded section of architect 0004 says so; T1.2 is the migration; edit the two sentences when the architect spec is approved |
| C2 | Search 0003 section 6 still says "`articles(search_vector_en)` GIN" and "no new trigram index"; ADR-0034 uses expression indexes and ADR-0035 adds a summary trigram index | Note | Section 3 and 14 were amended; fix section 6 wording in T1.5 |
| C3 | Architect 0004 FP-1/HP-2 describe an application stem function; stemming is now Postgres's English config | Note | Treat FP-1 as "stem collisions" only; HP-2 is void |
| C4 | ADR-0030 says "generated"; ADR-0034 supersedes that wording | Note | ADR-0034 governs |
| C5 | DBA 0001 says nothing updates `articles`; versions now update it (`0003_article_versions.sql`) | Note | The new partial index is maintained on update; covered by the version test |
| C6 | Telemetry reuses the `query` label key for index names and uses `kind` with different value sets on two metrics | Risk | Acceptable under the label allow-list; rename in a follow-up if confusing; T2.6 checks the label test |
| C7 | UX 0004 open question: `ArticleCard` sets `lang` of the AI summary from the article language, wrong if the summary is English | Risk | T2.2 checks and fixes `lang="en"` for summaries if Q1 is yes |
| C8 | Search on summaries only works after enrichment; unenriched articles miss summary matches | Risk | Coverage line (T2.4); P3 |
| C9 | The `articles` partial index predicate must be repeated textually by the query | Risk | Plan test P7 (T1.6) |
| C10 | Quoted-term matching on summaries has no dedicated index (rechecked on narrowed rows) | Risk | Experiment E9 in T1.6; add an index only if the plan test shows a problem |
| C11 | Late decision: foreign originals are not English-stemmed. Recall for English words inside foreign originals depends on the substring branch | Note | Golden cases G8, G14 document it |
| C12 | Unvalidated assumptions from the context file: real foreign share, article size, PostgreSQL extension permissions | Risk | First experiment in T1.6 replaces the guesses |
No principle conflict is unrecorded: P3 over P4 (broader default) is ADR-0033; precision path is ADR-0031.

## 5. Dependency graph
| Task | Depends on |
| --- | --- |
| T1.1 Seed helper and fixtures | none |
| T1.2 Migration 0007 | T1.1 (for the test) |
| T1.3 Migration test | T1.2 |
| T1.4 Compiler and operator-matrix tests | none (parallel with T1.2) |
| T1.5 List query and match sides | T1.2, T1.4 |
| T1.6 Integration golden and plan tests | T1.3, T1.5 |
| T1.7 Benchmark B1 and review gate | T1.6 |
| T2.1 Headline-pair function | none (can start in phase 1) |
| T2.2 Search card | T1.5, T2.1 |
| T2.3 Article page | T2.1 |
| T2.4 Echo, notes, strings, coverage line | T1.4 |
| T2.5 Matched-side marker | T1.5 |
| T2.6 Beacon, metrics, alerts, dashboards | T1.5, T2.3 |
| T2.7 End-to-end keyboard and no-JS tests | T2.2, T2.3 |
| T2.8 Benchmark B2, review gate, spec close-out | T2.2 to T2.7 |
```
T1.1 → T1.2 → T1.3 ─┐
T1.4 ───────────────┼→ T1.5 → T1.6 → T1.7 → [phase 2]
T2.1 ─(parallel)────┘
```
Critical path: T1.1, T1.2, T1.5, T1.6, then T2.2/T2.5, T2.7, T2.8. Parallel: T1.4 and T2.1 can run beside the migration work (different files).

## 6. Phases

### Phase 1: Search data layer and query (about 12 to 16 hours)
Goal: unquoted Latin terms find English word forms and partial words across original, translation and summary, quoted terms stay exact, and plans use the new indexes.
Entry criteria: ADR-0030 to 0035 accepted (done); no blockers.
Rollback or safe-stop: drop the four indexes concurrently; the compiler change is behind the same commit, so revert it too. Search then returns to the previous behaviour; no data changed.
Human checkpoints: T1.6 plan inspection; T1.7 benchmark review.

**T1.1 Add seeding helper and fixtures** (agent, 1 to 2 h)
- Why: plan tests and golden cases need 20,000+ articles with foreign rows, translations and summaries (testing 0004 sections 3.1, 7).
- Steps: extend `tests/harness/db.ts` with a seeded bulk loader; extend `tests/fixtures/articles.ts` and `tests/fixtures/translation.ts` with inflection pairs (startup/startups, enterprise/enterprises, news), `und` and `en-GB` labels, Arabic/French/Chinese rows, current and non-current summaries via `derived_values`; reuse the seeded generator in `.benchmarks/article-ingest/bench-lib.mjs`.
- Where: `tests/harness/db.ts`, `tests/fixtures/`.
- Output: a helper that seeds N rows with a fixed seed and runs `ANALYZE`.
- Acceptance: deterministic row counts across two runs; foreign share 30 percent.
- Depends on: none. Spec refs: testing 0004 sections 3.1, 7.

**T1.2 Write migration 0007: four concurrent expression indexes** (agent, 2 to 3 h)
- Why: ADR-0030, 0034, 0035; DBA 0004 sections 4 and 4.1; FP-DB1 to FP-DB4.
- Steps: new `db/migrations/0007_english_search_indexes.sql` starting with `-- no-transaction`. `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` for: `articles_fts_en_idx` (`to_tsvector('english', search_text)` where `split_part(language, '-', 1) IN ('en','und')`), `article_translations_fts_en_idx` (same expression, `WHERE superseded_at IS NULL`), `derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx` (`to_tsvector('english', value)` where `field = 'summary' AND is_current`), `derived_values_summary_trgm_idx` (`gin_trgm_ops`, same predicate; skip with the `trgm_index` flag when `pg_trgm` is off). After building, drop any index with `indisvalid = false` first (re-run safe) and fail if one remains invalid. Run `pg_get_keywords()` on the new identifiers.
- Where: `db/migrations/`; the runner in `src/lib/db/migrate.ts` already supports `-- no-transaction`.
- Acceptance: migration applies on an empty and on a seeded database; all four indexes valid; rerun is a no-op.
- Depends on: none (test in T1.3). Estimate note: build time on a large table is unknown (FP-DB3).

**T1.3 Test the migration** (agent, 1 to 1.5 h)
- Steps: `tests/integration/migration-0007.test.ts` per testing 0004 section 3.5 (no-transaction applies, indexes valid, interrupted-build leftover handled, inserts continue during build, drop rollback, build time recorded on 100k rows).
- Acceptance: test passes; recorded build time on the seed.
- Depends on: T1.1, T1.2.

**T1.4 Change the compiler and write the operator-matrix tests** (agent, 3 to 4 h)
- Why: ADR-0031, 0033, 0035; search 0003 sections 4, 12; FP-2, FP-3, FP-8, FP-S5 to S8.
- Steps: in `src/lib/search/leaf.ts` and `compile.ts`: classify unquoted Latin terms of 3+ characters as `stem_sub`, under 3 as `short_stem` (stem only), quoted as `exact`, non-Latin unchanged. Emit for each side the exact index expressions (original side repeats the `split_part(...) IN ('en','und')` predicate; foreign originals use the substring and exact paths only), the translation side with `superseded_at IS NULL`, the summary side as an `EXISTS` over `derived_values` with `field = 'summary' AND is_current`. Use `plainto_tsquery('english', $n)` parameters. Stop-word-only terms fall back to substring or exact. NOT stays original-only (never stem OR summary). Return per-side predicates so `matched_in` can report a set.
- Where: `src/lib/search/leaf.ts`, `compile.ts`, `parse.ts` (no grammar change), tests in `tests/unit/search-compile-translation.test.ts` and `tests/unit/parse.test.ts`.
- Acceptance: operator-by-side matrix in testing 0004 section 3.2 passes; no string-built tsquery; expression text snapshot equals the migration text.
- Depends on: none. Human gate: read the generated SQL for one multi-term query.

**T1.5 Update the list query and match sides** (agent, 2 to 3 h)
- Steps: in `src/lib/search/run.ts` add `left(tr.body_en, 600) AS body_excerpt_en`; replace the single `matched_in` with a set of sides (`original`, `translation`, `summary`) computed only for returned rows; keep keyset ordering. Expose `trgm_index` state to the search page response. Update the Search 0003 section 6 wording (C2).
- Where: `src/lib/search/run.ts`, `src/app/api/search/route.ts`, types used by `src/components/search/SearchPage.tsx`.
- Acceptance: response contains `body_excerpt_en` and `matched_in` sides; EXPLAIN shows the `CASE` is not evaluated for non-returned rows (E7 timing check).
- Depends on: T1.2, T1.4. Also verify in `src/worker/finish.ts` that a new summary flips the previous `is_current` (FP-DB6); fix only if wrong.

**T1.6 Golden, plan and experiment tests** (agent with a human reading the plans, 3 to 4 h)
- Steps: `tests/integration/search-default-match.test.ts` (G1 to G17), `tests/integration/search-plans.test.ts` (P1 to P7, node-type assertions on a 20k seed), experiments E2 to E5, E9 to E11 recorded in `reports/` with environment details; run the first sizing experiment (index sizes and build times) and replace the guesses in DBA 0004 section 3; check 20 real summaries for language (Q1).
- Acceptance: all cases pass; recall 100 percent on G1, G3, G8; extra-hit report produced.
- Human checkpoint: a person reads the plans for stem OR substring, NOT, rare and common terms and chooses OR/EXISTS versus the UNION shape (HP-1, HP-S1, HP-DB2).
- Depends on: T1.3, T1.5.

**T1.7 Benchmark B1 and review gate** (agent runs; human decides, 1 to 1.5 h)
- Steps: extend `.benchmarks/article-ingest/` (carma-benchmark) to compare insert rows/s with and without the four indexes at 100k rows; run carma-review on the diff.
- Acceptance: within 15 percent (proposed) or the cost is reported and accepted by the user (Q5).
- Depends on: T1.6.
Phase 1 exit: migration, compiler, query and tests pass; B1 recorded; review report written.

### Phase 2: Display, echo, telemetry (about 10 to 15 hours)
Goal: English-first cards and article page, honest echo and match markers, signals and tests.
Entry criteria: Phase 1 exit; Q1 answered or defaulted.
Rollback or safe-stop: UI changes are independent per component; reverting the card or page returns the old layout without affecting search.
Human checkpoints: T2.2 look at cards with Arabic and Chinese data; T2.8 review.

**T2.1 Write the headline-pair function** (agent, 1 to 1.5 h)
- Why: ADR-0032; FP-6, FP-7. Steps: pure function returning primary, secondary, language codes and note for every UX 0004 section 5.2 state, reusing the job-state mapping in `src/lib/translate/display.ts`. Tests: `tests/unit/headline-pair.test.ts`, extend `tests/unit/translate-display.test.ts`.
- Acceptance: all state rows covered; never an empty primary. Depends on: none.

**T2.2 Rebuild the search card** (agent, 2 to 3 h)
- Steps: `src/components/ArticleCard.tsx`: English `h2` with `lang="en"`, original line labelled "Original (Arabic):", "Machine translated" tag (Q3), state notes, "Show more" → English excerpt, "Show original text" → original excerpt underneath, no-JS handling, summary `lang` fix (C7). Retire `englishHeadline` and related strings in `src/lib/ui/strings.ts`.
- Acceptance: component tests (testing 0004 section 3.3) pass; manual look at Arabic and Chinese cards at phone and desktop widths.
- Depends on: T1.5, T2.1.

**T2.3 Rebuild the article-page text block** (agent, 2 h)
- Steps: `src/components/TranslatedText.tsx` and `src/app/articles/[id]/page.tsx`: headline pair, English body, native `<details>` revealing the original underneath (translation stays visible), remove swap and min-height trick, live announcement, beacon on `toggle`.
- Acceptance: stacked content, keyboard operable, works with JavaScript disabled. Depends on: T2.1.

**T2.4 Echo, notes, strings, coverage line** (agent, 1.5 to 2 h)
- Steps: `src/lib/search/echo.ts` and `SearchPage.tsx`: quoted terms in quotes, loose-match note only with an unquoted Latin term, quote tip, changed NOT note, degraded-mode note, no-summary coverage line (Q2). Strings in `src/lib/ui/strings.ts`.
- Acceptance: echo tests (testing 0004 section 3.4); XSS check on terms. Depends on: T1.4.

**T2.5 Update the matched-side marker** (agent, 1 h)
- Steps: `src/components/MatchedInTag.tsx` for sets of sides and summary copy (UX 0004 section 5.5). Acceptance: marker text per combination. Depends on: T1.5.

**T2.6 Add beacon values, metrics, alerts, dashboards** (agent, 2 to 3 h)
- Steps: update the route `src/app/api/telemetry/translation-view/route.ts` (new values, keep legacy one release, Q6); add series in `src/lib/metrics.ts` (check `tests/unit/metrics-labels.test.ts`); emit from compiler, search route and status refresher; alerts E1 to E3 in `ops/alerts.yml`; Grafana search row in `ops/grafana/`; log fields without query text.
- Acceptance: beacon enum test (`tests/unit/translation-view-route.test.ts`); series visible on `/api/metrics`; alert rules load. Depends on: T1.5, T2.3.

**T2.7 End-to-end tests** (agent, 1 to 1.5 h)
- Steps: Playwright: keyboard toggles, focus stays, no-JS article page reveal, card two-level reveal, RTL fixture. Where: `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` or a new spec. Depends on: T2.2, T2.3.

**T2.8 Benchmark B2, review gate, close-out** (agent plus human, 1.5 to 2 h)
- Steps: carma-benchmark for search latency by term kind (B2); carma-review on the phase diff; update README search syntax section; ask the user to approve the architect spec 0004 (then set approved and fix C1, C3).
- Acceptance: B2 within thresholds in testing 0004 section 5; review report in `.specs/review/`.
- Depends on: T2.2 to T2.7.
Phase 2 exit: all tests in testing 0004 section 11 pass.

## 7. Traceability matrix
| Requirement / ID | Task | Proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English headline first, original underneath (ADR-0032) | T2.1, T2.2, T2.3 | headline-pair and component tests, e2e |
| English text first, original on request | T2.3 | component test, e2e no-JS |
| "startups" finds "startup" (ADR-0030, 0033) | T1.4, T1.5, T1.6 | G1, G3, plan P1 |
| Exact in quotes (ADR-0031) | T1.4, T2.4 | G2, echo tests |
| Summaries searchable (ADR-0035) | T1.2, T1.4, T1.5 | G13, G16, G17, P6 |
| Stem scope (ADR-0035) | T1.4 | G14, G15, P7 |
| FP-1 | T1.6 | collision report |
| FP-2, FP-S5 | T1.4, T1.6 | matrix, G1, G5 |
| FP-3 | T1.6 | G10, P3 |
| FP-4 | T1.6, T2.4 | flag-off test, note test |
| FP-5 | T1.4, T1.6 | G7 |
| FP-6 | T2.1, T1.6 | G9 |
| FP-7 | T2.1, T2.2 | headline-pair, component tests |
| FP-8, FP-S6 | T1.4, T1.6 | G2 |
| FP-9 | T2.3, T2.7 | no-JS and keyboard e2e |
| FP-S7, FP-DB5 | T1.4, T1.6 | G6 |
| FP-S8 | T1.4 | placeholder assertions |
| FP-S9, FP-DB1, FP-DB4 | T1.4, T1.6 | P1, P2, P7 |
| FP-DB2, FP-DB3 | T1.2, T1.3 | migration test |
| FP-DB6, FP-DB7 | T1.5, T1.6 | G17, Q1 check |
| FP-S10 | T1.6 | extra-hit report |
| HP-1, HP-S1, HP-DB2 | T1.6, T2.8 | plans, B2 |
| HP-DB1, HP-S2 | T1.7 | B1 |
| Telemetry signals | T2.6 | beacon test, label test, `/api/metrics` |
No empty cells. HP-2 is void (C3).

## 8. Risks and assumptions
- Estimates: 22 to 31 hours; widest uncertainty is migration build time and plan tuning in T1.2 and T1.6 (plan shape may force the UNION alternative and a second pass).
- Assumed: PostgreSQL 16.6 with `pg_trgm`; summaries are English; the PoC rate (0.58/s), so the 800/s write cost is extrapolation only.
- The partial `articles` index and language predicate is the most fragile part (C9).
- Over-matching is a deliberate P3 trade; users have quotes.

## 9. Execution notes
- Work tasks in dependency order; report each task done with its acceptance evidence. If a plan test fails or B1 misses, stop and return to carma-dba with the plan or timings rather than changing the design in place.
- If summary language turns out not to be English (Q1), return to carma-searchability for the summary side.
- After each phase run carma-benchmark and carma-review as the gate; the user decides on a missed threshold.
- Record any new binding decision as an ADR through carma-architect (next number 0036).

content.content:
1	---
2	spec: carma-plan
3	number: 0004
4	title: Plan for English-first display and default stemmed/substring search
5	status: draft
6	date: 2026-10-24
7	feature: english-first-substring-search
8	inputs: [.specs/architect/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0030-english-stemming-index-for-default-search.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0031-quoted-terms-are-exact-matches.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0032-english-first-display-with-original-underneath.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0033-unquoted-terms-match-stem-or-substring.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0034-english-stem-index-as-expression-index.md, .specs/architect/adrs/0035-stemming-scope-and-summaries-searchable.md, .specs/search/0003-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/data/dba/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/telemetry/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/ux/0004-english-first-substring-search.md, .specs/testing/backend/0004-english-first-substring-search.md]
9	principles: [P1, P3, P5, P7, P8]
10	supersedes: null
11	---
12	
13	# 0004 Plan for English-first display and default stemmed/substring search
14	
15	## 1. Summary
16	Build two changes on the shipped translation feature: (1) English-first headlines and text with the original underneath, and (2) default search that matches English word forms and partial words, with quotes for exact matches and summaries made searchable. Two phases, about 22 to 31 hours in total. Critical path: migration (four concurrent indexes) → compiler → list query → plan tests → UI. The database and query work (phase 1) must land before the UI (phase 2) can show matched sides and English excerpts.
17	
18	## 2. Inputs
19	All specs and ADRs in the front matter, present and read. Skipped by choice: carma-devops (nothing new to run; the migration-at-start-up concern is a task here) and carma-data-sanity (ILIKE escaping and escaped rendering are covered in test tasks). Mode: sequential. Specs were amended in place (still drafts) after the late decisions in ADR-0035; they were not re-run.
20	
21	## 3. Blockers and open questions
22	No blockers. Open items to track (all have a safe default):
23	| # | Item | Owner | Default if unanswered |
24	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
25	| Q1 | Summary language: assumed English | Human, check 20 real summaries in phase 1 | English |
26	| Q2 | Wording of the "no summary yet" coverage line | Human | Wording in UX 0004 section 5.5 |
27	| Q3 | "Machine translated" tag on every translated card | Human | Every card |
28	| Q4 | `pg_trgm` enabled in the target database | Human, T1.2 | Flag `trgm_index` decides at runtime |
29	| Q5 | Index size and write cost at 800/s | Human, after B1 | Extrapolation only, labelled |
30	| Q6 | Keep legacy beacon values one release | Human | Keep |
31	
32	## 4. Consistency report
33	| # | Finding | Class | Resolution |
34	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
35	| C1 | Architect 0004 sections 1 and 5.3 say "no migration expected"; ADR-0030/0034/0035 require migration 0007 | Note | Decisions recorded section of architect 0004 says so; T1.2 is the migration; edit the two sentences when the architect spec is approved |
36	| C2 | Search 0003 section 6 still says "`articles(search_vector_en)` GIN" and "no new trigram index"; ADR-0034 uses expression indexes and ADR-0035 adds a summary trigram index | Note | Section 3 and 14 were amended; fix section 6 wording in T1.5 |
37	| C3 | Architect 0004 FP-1/HP-2 describe an application stem function; stemming is now Postgres's English config | Note | Treat FP-1 as "stem collisions" only; HP-2 is void |
38	| C4 | ADR-0030 says "generated"; ADR-0034 supersedes that wording | Note | ADR-0034 governs |
39	| C5 | DBA 0001 says nothing updates `articles`; versions now update it (`0003_article_versions.sql`) | Note | The new partial index is maintained on update; covered by the version test |
40	| C6 | Telemetry reuses the `query` label key for index names and uses `kind` with different value sets on two metrics | Risk | Acceptable under the label allow-list; rename in a follow-up if confusing; T2.6 checks the label test |
41	| C7 | UX 0004 open question: `ArticleCard` sets `lang` of the AI summary from the article language, wrong if the summary is English | Risk | T2.2 checks and fixes `lang="en"` for summaries if Q1 is yes |
42	| C8 | Search on summaries only works after enrichment; unenriched articles miss summary matches | Risk | Coverage line (T2.4); P3 |
43	| C9 | The `articles` partial index predicate must be repeated textually by the query | Risk | Plan test P7 (T1.6) |
44	| C10 | Quoted-term matching on summaries has no dedicated index (rechecked on narrowed rows) | Risk | Experiment E9 in T1.6; add an index only if the plan test shows a problem |
45	| C11 | Late decision: foreign originals are not English-stemmed. Recall for English words inside foreign originals depends on the substring branch | Note | Golden cases G8, G14 document it |
46	| C12 | Unvalidated assumptions from the context file: real foreign share, article size, PostgreSQL extension permissions | Risk | First experiment in T1.6 replaces the guesses |
47	No principle conflict is unrecorded: P3 over P4 (broader default) is ADR-0033; precision path is ADR-0031.
48	
49	## 5. Dependency graph
50	| Task | Depends on |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| T1.1 Seed helper and fixtures | none |
53	| T1.2 Migration 0007 | T1.1 (for the test) |
54	| T1.3 Migration test | T1.2 |
55	| T1.4 Compiler and operator-matrix tests | none (parallel with T1.2) |
56	| T1.5 List query and match sides | T1.2, T1.4 |
57	| T1.6 Integration golden and plan tests | T1.3, T1.5 |
58	| T1.7 Benchmark B1 and review gate | T1.6 |
59	| T2.1 Headline-pair function | none (can start in phase 1) |
60	| T2.2 Search card | T1.5, T2.1 |
61	| T2.3 Article page | T2.1 |
62	| T2.4 Echo, notes, strings, coverage line | T1.4 |
63	| T2.5 Matched-side marker | T1.5 |
64	| T2.6 Beacon, metrics, alerts, dashboards | T1.5, T2.3 |
65	| T2.7 End-to-end keyboard and no-JS tests | T2.2, T2.3 |
66	| T2.8 Benchmark B2, review gate, spec close-out | T2.2 to T2.7 |
67	```
68	T1.1 → T1.2 → T1.3 ─┐
69	T1.4 ───────────────┼→ T1.5 → T1.6 → T1.7 → [phase 2]
70	T2.1 ─(parallel)────┘
71	```
72	Critical path: T1.1, T1.2, T1.5, T1.6, then T2.2/T2.5, T2.7, T2.8. Parallel: T1.4 and T2.1 can run beside the migration work (different files).
73	
74	## 6. Phases
75	
76	### Phase 1: Search data layer and query (about 12 to 16 hours)
77	Goal: unquoted Latin terms find English word forms and partial words across original, translation and summary, quoted terms stay exact, and plans use the new indexes.
78	Entry criteria: ADR-0030 to 0035 accepted (done); no blockers.
79	Rollback or safe-stop: drop the four indexes concurrently; the compiler change is behind the same commit, so revert it too. Search then returns to the previous behaviour; no data changed.
80	Human checkpoints: T1.6 plan inspection; T1.7 benchmark review.
81	
82	**T1.1 Add seeding helper and fixtures** (agent, 1 to 2 h)
83	- Why: plan tests and golden cases need 20,000+ articles with foreign rows, translations and summaries (testing 0004 sections 3.1, 7).
84	- Steps: extend `tests/harness/db.ts` with a seeded bulk loader; extend `tests/fixtures/articles.ts` and `tests/fixtures/translation.ts` with inflection pairs (startup/startups, enterprise/enterprises, news), `und` and `en-GB` labels, Arabic/French/Chinese rows, current and non-current summaries via `derived_values`; reuse the seeded generator in `.benchmarks/article-ingest/bench-lib.mjs`.
85	- Where: `tests/harness/db.ts`, `tests/fixtures/`.
86	- Output: a helper that seeds N rows with a fixed seed and runs `ANALYZE`.
87	- Acceptance: deterministic row counts across two runs; foreign share 30 percent.
88	- Depends on: none. Spec refs: testing 0004 sections 3.1, 7.
89	
90	**T1.2 Write migration 0007: four concurrent expression indexes** (agent, 2 to 3 h)
91	- Why: ADR-0030, 0034, 0035; DBA 0004 sections 4 and 4.1; FP-DB1 to FP-DB4.
92	- Steps: new `db/migrations/0007_english_search_indexes.sql` starting with `-- no-transaction`. `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` for: `articles_fts_en_idx` (`to_tsvector('english', search_text)` where `split_part(language, '-', 1) IN ('en','und')`), `article_translations_fts_en_idx` (same expression, `WHERE superseded_at IS NULL`), `derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx` (`to_tsvector('english', value)` where `field = 'summary' AND is_current`), `derived_values_summary_trgm_idx` (`gin_trgm_ops`, same predicate; skip with the `trgm_index` flag when `pg_trgm` is off). After building, drop any index with `indisvalid = false` first (re-run safe) and fail if one remains invalid. Run `pg_get_keywords()` on the new identifiers.
93	- Where: `db/migrations/`; the runner in `src/lib/db/migrate.ts` already supports `-- no-transaction`.
94	- Acceptance: migration applies on an empty and on a seeded database; all four indexes valid; rerun is a no-op.
95	- Depends on: none (test in T1.3). Estimate note: build time on a large table is unknown (FP-DB3).
96	
97	**T1.3 Test the migration** (agent, 1 to 1.5 h)
98	- Steps: `tests/integration/migration-0007.test.ts` per testing 0004 section 3.5 (no-transaction applies, indexes valid, interrupted-build leftover handled, inserts continue during build, drop rollback, build time recorded on 100k rows).
99	- Acceptance: test passes; recorded build time on the seed.
100	- Depends on: T1.1, T1.2.
101	
102	**T1.4 Change the compiler and write the operator-matrix tests** (agent, 3 to 4 h)
103	- Why: ADR-0031, 0033, 0035; search 0003 sections 4, 12; FP-2, FP-3, FP-8, FP-S5 to S8.
104	- Steps: in `src/lib/search/leaf.ts` and `compile.ts`: classify unquoted Latin terms of 3+ characters as `stem_sub`, under 3 as `short_stem` (stem only), quoted as `exact`, non-Latin unchanged. Emit for each side the exact index expressions (original side repeats the `split_part(...) IN ('en','und')` predicate; foreign originals use the substring and exact paths only), the translation side with `superseded_at IS NULL`, the summary side as an `EXISTS` over `derived_values` with `field = 'summary' AND is_current`. Use `plainto_tsquery('english', $n)` parameters. Stop-word-only terms fall back to substring or exact. NOT stays original-only (never stem OR summary). Return per-side predicates so `matched_in` can report a set.
105	- Where: `src/lib/search/leaf.ts`, `compile.ts`, `parse.ts` (no grammar change), tests in `tests/unit/search-compile-translation.test.ts` and `tests/unit/parse.test.ts`.

-- no-transaction
-- English stemmed expression indexes (ADR-0030/0034/0035) and summary trigram.
-- Rollback: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS articles_fts_en_idx;
--           DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS article_translations_fts_en_idx;
--           DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx;
--           DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS derived_values_summary_trgm_idx;

-- Drop invalid leftovers from an interrupted concurrent build (re-run safe).
DO $$
DECLARE
  r record;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN
    SELECT c.relname AS indexname
      FROM pg_index i
      JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
     WHERE c.relname IN (
       'articles_fts_en_idx',
       'article_translations_fts_en_idx',
       'derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx',
       'derived_values_summary_trgm_idx'
     )
       AND NOT i.indisvalid
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS %I', r.indexname);
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- Reserved-word check on new identifiers (must not be SQL keywords).
DO $$
DECLARE
  names text[] := ARRAY[
    'articles_fts_en_idx',
    'article_translations_fts_en_idx',
    'derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx',
    'derived_values_summary_trgm_idx'
  ];
  n text;
BEGIN
  FOREACH n IN ARRAY names LOOP
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_get_keywords() k WHERE k.word = lower(n) AND k.catcode = 'R') THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'identifier % is a reserved keyword', n;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS articles_fts_en_idx
  ON articles USING GIN (to_tsvector('english', search_text))
  WHERE split_part(language, '-', 1) IN ('en', 'und');

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS article_translations_fts_en_idx
  ON article_translations USING GIN (to_tsvector('english', search_text))
  WHERE superseded_at IS NULL;

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx
  ON derived_values USING GIN (to_tsvector('english', value))
  WHERE field = 'summary' AND is_current;

-- Summary trigram: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside DO/EXCEPTION.
-- When pg_trgm is unavailable the statement fails; mirror 0001 by catching via a
-- non-concurrent fallback only when the concurrent form is not usable.
-- Prefer concurrent when the extension is present (normal path).
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS derived_values_summary_trgm_idx
  ON derived_values USING GIN (value gin_trgm_ops)
  WHERE field = 'summary' AND is_current;

-- Fail loudly if any required index is missing or invalid after build.
DO $$
DECLARE
  bad text;
BEGIN
  SELECT string_agg(c.relname, ', ')
    INTO bad
    FROM pg_index i
    JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
   WHERE c.relname IN (
     'articles_fts_en_idx',
     'article_translations_fts_en_idx',
     'derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx',
     'derived_values_summary_trgm_idx'
   )
     AND NOT i.indisvalid;
  IF bad IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid search index(es) after migration 0007: %', bad;
  END IF;

  IF to_regclass('public.articles_fts_en_idx') IS NULL
     OR to_regclass('public.article_translations_fts_en_idx') IS NULL
     OR to_regclass('public.derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx') IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'required English FTS index missing after migration 0007';
  END IF;
END $$;

-- no-transaction
-- English stemmed expression indexes (ADR-0030/0034/0035) and summary trigram.
-- Rollback: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS articles_fts_en_idx;
--           DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS article_translations_fts_en_idx;
--           DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx;
--           DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS derived_values_summary_trgm_idx;

-- Drop invalid leftovers from an interrupted concurrent build (re-run safe).
DO $$
DECLARE
  r record;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN
    SELECT c.relname AS indexname
      FROM pg_index i
      JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
     WHERE c.relname IN (
       'articles_fts_en_idx',
       'article_translations_fts_en_idx',
       'derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx',
       'derived_values_summary_trgm_idx'
     )
       AND NOT i.indisvalid
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS %I', r.indexname);
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- Reserved-word check on new identifiers (must not be SQL keywords).
DO $$
DECLARE
  names text[] := ARRAY[
    'articles_fts_en_idx',
    'article_translations_fts_en_idx',
    'derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx',
    'derived_values_summary_trgm_idx'
  ];
  n text;
BEGIN
  FOREACH n IN ARRAY names LOOP
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_get_keywords() k WHERE k.word = lower(n) AND k.catcode = 'R') THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'identifier % is a reserved keyword', n;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS articles_fts_en_idx
  ON articles USING GIN (to_tsvector('english', search_text))
  WHERE split_part(language, '-', 1) IN ('en', 'und');

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS article_translations_fts_en_idx
  ON article_translations USING GIN (to_tsvector('english', search_text))
  WHERE superseded_at IS NULL;

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx
  ON derived_values USING GIN (to_tsvector('english', value))
  WHERE field = 'summary' AND is_current;

-- Summary trigram: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside DO/EXCEPTION.
-- When pg_trgm is unavailable the statement fails; mirror 0001 by catching via a
-- non-concurrent fallback only when the concurrent form is not usable.
-- Prefer concurrent when the extension is present (normal path).
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS derived_values_summary_trgm_idx
  ON derived_values USING GIN (value gin_trgm_ops)
  WHERE field = 'summary' AND is_current;

DECLARE
  bad text;
BEGIN
  SELECT string_agg(c.relname, ', ')
    INTO bad
    FROM pg_index i
    JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
   WHERE c.relname IN (
     'articles_fts_en_idx',
     'article_translations_fts_en_idx',
     'derived_values_summary_fts_en_idx',
     'derived_values_summary_trgm_idx'
   )

# 0005 Review: English-first search (plan 0004) and commit gate

## 1. Verdict and summary

**Approve with changes.** No secret would be committed, and no silent data-loss path was found. Two items need a fix or a check before the phase gate closes.

What was reviewed: the repository has **no commits** (`git log` fails), so there is no diff. I reviewed the whole untracked tree as "what would be committed", with the code read focused on plan 0004: `db/migrations/0007_english_search_indexes.sql`, `src/lib/search/{leaf,compile,run}.ts`, the `is_current` flip in `src/worker/finish.ts`. I did not read the UI components, telemetry wiring or e2e tests in this pass.

Top findings:
1. **Should fix.** Stop-word term `the` (and any stop word of 3+ chars) registers a bind parameter that no SQL references (`compile.ts:244-246`). PostgreSQL normally rejects this with "could not determine data type of parameter $n". Not run here; integration case G6 (`search-default-match.test.ts:155`) should expose it if it runs against a database. The unit test only checks that `ILIKE` appears.
2. **Should fix.** `/api/search` runs 6 or more extra queries per request, several of them whole-table counts, so the cost grows with the corpus. The `excluded_by_filter_not_enriched` coverage figure is always 0, which breaks P3 coverage honesty.
3. **Gate still open.** Plan T1.6 (human EXPLAIN read) and T1.7 (benchmark B1, at 15 percent) have no recorded results; `reports/english-search-phase1.md` says "Record results here when executed".

## 2. Scope reviewed

- Revision: none. No commits exist, so the working tree is the change. 30-odd top-level entries are untracked.
- Plan: `.specs/plan/0004`. Specs and ADRs: ADR-0030 to 0035, `.specs/architect/0004`, DBA and search 0004, telemetry 0004 (listed in the plan front matter). I used the plan's own summary of those ADRs rather than re-reading every one.
- Earlier review `0004-english-first-substring-search.md` (short checklist) was read; this report does not supersede it.
- Not run: the test suites, the benchmark, EXPLAIN. Statements about test results are taken from the repo's own report and are unverified.

## 3. Plan conformance

| Task | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1.2 Migration 0007 | Delivered | Four `CONCURRENTLY` indexes, `-- no-transaction`, invalid leftovers dropped, post-check |
| T1.3 Migration test | Present | `tests/integration/migration-0007.test.ts` exists; not run |
| T1.4 Compiler and matrix | Delivered | `compile.ts`, `leaf.ts`; expression text shared in `EXPR` (FP-DB1) |
| T1.5 List query, sides | Delivered | `run.ts:101-129` `body_excerpt_en`, `matched_in` set; `trgm_index` exposed |
| FP-DB6 `is_current` flip | Delivered | `finish.ts:174` flips `summary` and `topic` |
| T1.6 Golden and plan tests | Partly | Files exist (`search-default-match`, `search-plans`); human plan reading and E2 to E5 reports not recorded |
| T1.7 Benchmark B1 | Not delivered | README section exists; no result recorded; Q5 open |
| Phase 2 (UI, telemetry, e2e) | Not reviewed | Out of this pass |
| Scope creep | None found in files read | |

## 4. Trade-off and spec conformance

| Decision | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADR-0031 quoted = exact | Respected | `classifyLeaf` quoted single word is `exact`, multi-word is `phrase` |
| ADR-0033 unquoted = stem OR substring | Respected | `compile.ts:243-263` |
| ADR-0027/0035 NOT is original-only | Respected | `compile.ts:272-278` |
| ADR-0034 expression indexes, text must match | Respected, fragile | `EXPR` strings equal the migration text; the `articles` predicate is repeated by hand (plan C9); the plan test P7 is the guard |
| PostgreSQL only | Respected | No new infrastructure |
| P3 completeness (no dropped item) | Respected in search | Stop-word fallback goes to substring, not to "no results" |
| P5 language neutrality | Respected with a caveat | Foreign originals are not English-stemmed by design (ADR-0035, C11); non-Latin goes to substring; script detection covers Arabic and CJK ranges only, so Cyrillic, Greek and Hebrew terms would be treated as Latin and stemmed with the English config |
| Parameterised queries | Respected | All terms are bind params; ILIKE escaped by `escapeIlike`; wildcard term stripped to letters and digits |
| Telemetry for changed paths | Unverifiable here | Counter `mss_search_empty_stem_total` seen; rest in T2.6, not read |

## 5. Hot path review

Search compile and list query (HP-1, HP-S1, HP-DB2; not the ingest hot path):

- **Readable.** `compileTerm` is long but flat and explicit, and the per-kind branches are easy to follow. Suggestion: the `side` repetition (`if side === original ... translation ... summary ... both`) appears six times; a small table of `{orig, tr, sum}` builders per kind would remove about 60 lines without adding indirection. Optional.
- **Over-work per request (Should fix).** `run.ts:233-251` issues, after the list query: `computeCoverage` (4 queries, including `count(*) FROM articles` and two `count(DISTINCT article_id) FROM derived_values` over the whole corpus), `computeTranslationCoverage` (5 correlated counts), `computeSummaryMissing` (NOT EXISTS scan), the `system_flags` read, and optionally a count. All run sequentially with `await`. At 69 million rows a day these cannot be per request. Suggestion: reuse the `metrics-refresh` worker to cache corpus-wide counts, keep only the filter-dependent ones live, and run the remainder with `Promise.all`.

content.text:
Each coverage feature added its own query, and nobody asked whether the cost scales. I read `run.ts` for this review, so this comes from the code. I haven't measured it.

**Where the queries come from.** After the main list query, `runSearch` also runs:

| Query | Why it exists | Depends on the search? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `derived_values` and `enrichment_jobs` lookups | Card data for the returned page only | Yes, but bounded by the page size, so cheap |
| `computeCoverage`, part 1: `count(*)` with the base filters | The "N articles in range" line | Yes, filters only |
| `computeCoverage`, part 2: `count(*) FROM articles`, plus two `count(DISTINCT article_id) FROM derived_values` and two `max()` calls | Corpus coverage and the freshness watermark | **No, the same answer for every request** |
| `computeTranslationCoverage` | The translated, queued and failed breakdown | Filters only |
| `computeSummaryMissing` | The "N articles have no summary yet" note (plan C8) | Filters only |
| `system_flags` read | The "partial-word matching is slow" note | No |
| Optional `count(*)` | Only when `includeTotal` is set | Yes |

The motive is a good one. Principle P3 says a user should be able to tell "no results" from "not covered" from "not yet processed". ADR-0035 makes summaries searchable, which creates a new gap: articles without a summary can't match on one. The coverage queries are how the UI says so honestly. The design problem is that every one of these is computed live, on every search, and they run one after another.

**Why the table counts are the real concern.** Part 2 of `computeCoverage` ignores your filters entirely. It answers the same question on every request but rescans the whole corpus each time. At 800 articles a second that's 69 million rows a day, so a `count(DISTINCT)` over `derived_values` will go from milliseconds to seconds. Search latency then depends on corpus size, and your own statement timeout would start returning 503s. The existing `metrics-refresh` worker could compute these every minute or so, and the search request would just read them.

**The honesty problem, specifically.** Two things in `computeCoverage` give wrong or misleading numbers:
- `excluded_by_filter_not_enriched` always comes out 0. It subtracts a query from an identical copy of itself, and the comment says "approximate… skip heavy calc". A constant 0 reads as "your enrichment filter excluded nothing", which may not be true.
- `articles_in_scope` is the whole-corpus total, not the number in scope after your filters. I should have called this out in the report. I missed it the first time.

I'm not sure where the numbers are rendered in the UI, because I didn't read the Phase 2 components. If they're shown by default, as P6 and P3 imply, users are being shown figures that look precise and aren't.

**Suggested fix, in order:**
1. Remove or correctly compute `excluded_by_filter_not_enriched`, and rename or fix `articles_in_scope`. This is the cheap, high-value one.
2. Move the filter-independent corpus counts and the watermark into the refresher.
3. Run the remaining queries with `Promise.all` instead of sequentially.

Say the word and I'll start with step 1 and then do the other two. Moving the counts to the worker is a design change, so I'd put it through a short ADR rather than just do it.

---
name: "carma-searchability"
description: "Designs how Carma article data is made searchable and analysable, building on the carma-architect output, including the analytical layer behind reports."
---

# carma-searchability

Search is the product's core job: data is prepared so that it can be found, and it will be searched constantly. A missed mention is the most damaging failure Carma has (P3), so this skill designs for recall first and speed second, then makes the cost of that choice visible.

Finding articles is half the job. Carma's reports also slice a set of articles into counts, shares, trends and rankings, and the reader has to be able to trust those numbers. The analytical layer is designed here too, because it decides what has to be stored and indexed at ingestion and cannot be retrofitted cheaply.

Read `references/carma-context.md` first for the principles, constraints and spec conventions. The Appendix at the end of this file is a checklist of the data points, grains and report patterns that analysis needs; use it as a checklist and extend it when the feature brings new report types.

## Inputs

Read the latest non-superseded `.specs/architect/NNNN-*.md` for this feature and the ADRs that reference it. You need: what is searched, by whom, how often, the data flow and states, and the failure and hot path registers (FP/HP). If there is no architect spec, ask the user to run carma-architect or, for a small request, run its analysis inline and say so.

First check applicability. If no requirement involves finding, filtering, matching or aggregating content, say that search design is not needed and stop. Do not invent a search problem.

## Workflow

### 1. Separate the three kinds of search

They look similar and have different cost profiles, so design them separately.

- **Ad hoc search.** An analyst types a query against the stored archive. Latency of seconds is fine, but queries are varied and frequent.
- **Standing queries.** Saved brand and keyword definitions that must be evaluated against every incoming article so mentions reach users within 15 minutes of `published_at` (P1). At 800 articles a second this is a reverse-search problem: the cost grows with the number of saved queries times arrivals. Matching at ingestion beats re-scanning the archive.
- **Analytical queries.** Report and dashboard questions: "what share of each market's coverage mentions X", "volume by month split by sentiment", "who was quoted most, and how negatively". They read many articles and return few numbers. Cost is driven by the number of articles in scope and the number of dimensions, so they are served from structures prepared at ingestion (step 7), not by scanning text.

For each, write down: who uses it, expected volume, acceptable latency, and the cost of a false negative versus a false positive. Carma's stated emphasis is not missing a mention, so false negatives cost more. Say so, then design for high recall with precision handled by ranking and review (P4), not by narrowing the match. For analytical queries the equivalent risk is a number that is wrong without looking wrong, so the cost to state is "a plausible but incorrect figure reaches a client".

Name the analytical questions the feature must answer. Take them from the requirements, and from the report patterns in the Appendix (section C). Each question later becomes a test (step 11).

### 2. Define the searchable document

List exactly what is indexed per article: `headline`, `body`, `source`, `published_at`, `language`, plus derived fields such as entities, topics and sentiment. For derived fields, carry their confidence and origin (P6, P7) so results can be filtered or ranked by them. State which fields are searched as text, which are filters, and which are only displayed.

Keep the extracted text as stored (raw markup is not retained by default). Normalised or tokenised forms are derived from it so they can be rebuilt when the method improves, and a result can always be traced to what was published (P8).

Headline and body are separate searchable fields. Some analysis is about the headline alone (emotive wording, "named in the headline"), and matching the body for those questions gives wrong answers.

### 3. Tokenization and normalisation, per language (P5)

The same data model must serve every language. Design a language-aware analysis step and a safe fallback, rather than special cases scattered through queries.

- **English and similar.** Case folding, stemming or lemmatisation, stop words. Decide whether brand names and short tokens (for example "AI") bypass stop words, because aggressive stop-word lists silently lose mentions.
- **Arabic.** Right-to-left. Normalise before indexing: strip diacritics and tatweel, unify alef and ya/alef maqsura variants, handle taa marbuta variation, and decide on light stemming. Prefixed articles and conjunctions attach to words, so a brand name inside a longer token must still match. Mixed Arabic and Latin text in one article is normal.
- **Chinese.** No spaces between words, so whitespace tokenisation finds nothing. Options: dictionary-based segmentation (accurate, needs a segmenter and a maintained dictionary, and brand names missing from it get split wrongly) or character n-grams (bigrams are a robust recall-first baseline, larger index). Simplified versus Traditional script variants may need conversion. Full-width and half-width forms need normalisation.
- **Any other language.** A documented fallback: Unicode normalisation (NFKC), case folding, and a language-agnostic tokenizer, with the article's `language` field and a detected language used to route it. State how the fallback behaves for scripts it cannot segment and how that shows up in coverage reporting.

Always apply one Unicode normalisation form consistently at index and query time. Mismatched normalisation is a classic reason a mention that is visibly there is not found.

Treat the `language` field as a claim, not a fact. Plan for a mismatch with the detected language and say what happens to those articles (still indexed, and flagged).

### 4. Entities, aliases and quotes

Brand and person mentions are the main thing Carma users search for and aggregate on, so entity handling is part of search, not an extra.

- **Entity resolution.** Each entity has a canonical id, a type (organisation, product, person, place), aliases per language, abbreviations, known misspellings, and links to parents and subsidiaries. Company and product are separate entities with a link (a product and its maker, a brand and its parent). Joint names ("A-B") must resolve to both. Expect spelling variants, abbreviations, two names for one organisation, and the same entity written differently in each language.
- **Match confidence (P6).** Resolution to an entity id carries a confidence and origin. Unresolved or low-confidence mentions stay findable by plain text; they are never dropped (P3).
- **Time-varying attributes.** Some entity facts change over time (a role, a status, a launch date). Store them with validity dates so "before launch" and "while CEO" can be asked.
- **Quotes as records.** A quote has its own text, speaker (entity), speaker role and type, polarity, topic, and span in the article. Quote text is searchable on its own. This is what allows "who was quoted most", "most negative speakers" and "what did X say about Y".

### 5. Indexing strategies on PostgreSQL

Present options with trade-offs and a recommendation, and check what the codebase and environment actually allow (version, extensions) before leaning on any of them. Candidates:

- Full-text search with `tsvector`/`tsquery` and GIN, using a text-search configuration per language where one exists and a `simple`-style configuration otherwise. Weigh storing the vector (fast query, bigger writes) versus computing it on the fly.
- Trigram matching (`pg_trgm`) for fuzzy names and misspellings; consider its fit for short strings and its index size.
- n-gram or bigram approaches for CJK where the built-in parser cannot segment.
- Extensions or an external search engine are possible but may not be allowed in Carma's environment. Name them as options for the user to rule in or out; do not assume them.

Indexing cost competes with ingestion throughput. Note where index maintenance sits on the write hot path and hand that concern to carma-dba explicitly.

### 6. Bucketing and partitioning

Bucketing exists so most queries touch a small slice of the data.

- **Time buckets** by `published_at` (hour or day) fit append-only data, allow cheap retention by dropping whole buckets, and match the recency bias of most queries. Consider hot, warm and cold tiers with different index richness: the newest bucket may carry lighter indexes so items become searchable sooner (P1), with fuller indexes built as it ages.
- **Language buckets** where analysis differs by language. Weigh the benefit of per-language indexes against the cost of cross-language queries.
- **Source buckets** only if source-scoped queries are common and the cardinality is manageable.
- **Standing-query buckets.** Group saved queries by shared terms so an incoming article is checked against a candidate set instead of every query: an inverted map from term to queries, or a multi-pattern matcher, followed by verification of the candidates.

For each bucketing choice state the query patterns it helps, the ones it hurts (cross-bucket queries), and the operational cost.

### 7. Analytical layer: grains, facets and aggregates

This step makes reports possible. Work from the Appendix and from the analytical questions named in step 1.

**7a. Grains.** List the grains the feature needs (article, headline, entity mention, quote, attribute reference, tag, event, external observation) and for each the fields, whether it is multi-valued, and which fields are derived. One article produces many child records, so they are separate tables or partitions linked to the article by id, never columns or arrays on the article row when the analysis counts them. State the expected child records per article, because that multiplies write volume at 800 articles a second. Hand that figure to carma-dba.

**7b. Dimensions and measures.** For each question list the dimensions to group and filter by, and the measures (count at which grain, share of which base, score, rank, trend). For every share, write the numerator, the denominator and the grain of each. If a question cannot name its denominator, it is not yet well defined: raise it as a decision.

**7c. Vocabularies and groupings.** Topics, concerns, attributes, commentator types and similar sets are controlled vocabularies: versioned data with labels per language, not code. Every coded value stores the vocabulary version. Region groupings are named, versioned sets of markets and may overlap; one market can sit in several groups.

**7d. Scope.** A scope is a saved, versioned definition: markets, outlets or tiers, interval (half-open, with a stated time zone rule), topic query, and whether it covers the full population or a sample. Every aggregate and every report cites its scope id. The same scope on the same data and vocabulary versions must give the same number.

**7e. How aggregates are served.** Present options with trade-offs and a recommendation:
- Compute on demand from the child records, using partition pruning and covering indexes. Simple and always exact; slow when scopes are large.
- Incremental rollups maintained at ingestion at the finest grain needed (for example day by market by entity by category by polarity), then rolled up for coarser views. Fast; adds write cost and a reconciliation need.
- Materialised views refreshed on a schedule. Cheap to build; stale between refreshes, so staleness must be shown.
- Extensions or an external column store. Name as options for the user to rule in or out.

Pick per question, not globally. Rollups must be rebuildable from the child records so a corrected coder or vocabulary can be re-applied (P8). Hand rollup maintenance cost to carma-dba and its reconciliation to carma-backend-testing.

**7f. Drill-through invariant.** Every aggregate must be turnable into the list of records that produced it, and the list size equals the count. Rollups therefore keep the keys or the scope needed to regenerate the list. Say how this works for each rollup (P8).

**7g. Honest numbers.** Design these in, do not leave them to the interface:
- Carry the base count (n) with every rate. Flag low n; do not hide small groups (P3).
- Carry enrichment coverage: of the articles in scope, how many have the coded field computed, and how many are low confidence or unresolved. A share computed over 40% of the scope must say so (P3, P6).
- Say whether numbers come from the full population or a sample.
- Store the comparison set and tie rule with every rank.
- Keep positive and negative counts separate; do not store only a signed net.
- Say what a score is about and its scale: sentiment toward a stated proposition versus general tone, with min, max and the meaning of the midpoint (P7).

**7h. External series and events.** Survey results, search-interest indexes and event annotations are stored apart from article data, labelled with source, market, term or question, wave or date, sample size and scale. Indexed series are comparable only within one pull. They join to article aggregates by market and time bucket; they never get written into article tables. Decide whether external data is in scope at all (decision for the user).

**7i. Time handling.** Choose the finest bucket needed (usually day), roll up to week and month, and state the time zone rule for month and day boundaries, because UTC and local boundaries put different articles in different buckets.

### 8. Ranking, relevance and confidence

Ranking must serve P4 (signal over volume) without hiding anything (P3). Combine text relevance, recency, and optionally source or entity weights. A relevance score from the database's ranking functions is not calibrated, so when it is shown it is expressed on the 0 to 100% scale with its origin and min/max range stated (P6, P7), and the interface can say "database text-rank score, uncalibrated". Never imply it is a probability.

Ranking entities in an analytical view (most quoted, highest share positive) is different from ranking articles; it follows rule 3 in the Appendix: state the comparison set, the minimum n, and the tie handling.

### 9. Deduplication and near-duplicates

Wire stories republished across outlets create near-duplicates. Cluster them (for example with content fingerprints) but keep every copy and the link between them. Collapsing in the results view is fine; deleting is not, because each source's copy is a distinct mention (P3, P8).

Decide, per analytical measure, whether duplicates count once or each time. A syndicated story in ten outlets is ten mentions but one story, and the report's number changes depending on the answer. State it in the measure's definition.

### 10. Freshness and coverage signalling

Search must tell the user the truth about what it can see. Design the index watermark (the `published_at` or ingest time up to which everything is searchable), per-language and per-source coverage, and the three distinct empty states: no match, not covered, not yet processed (P3). Define how the answer to "is this complete?" is computed.

Analytics adds a fourth state: **not yet enriched**. An article can be searchable before sentiment, entities or quotes are computed (P1), but aggregates over those fields only see enriched articles. Every aggregate reports its watermark and its enrichment coverage, so a number over a half-enriched hour is not read as final.

### 11. Recall, precision and aggregate evaluation plan

Without measurement, "high recall" is a hope. Specify a labelled evaluation set: planted mentions in English, Arabic and Chinese including inflected, prefixed, misspelled, transliterated and mixed-script variants, plus articles that should not match. Define target recall for standing queries, how it is measured per language, and how regressions are caught when a tokenizer or dictionary changes. This feeds carma-backend-testing.

Add, for the analytical layer:
- **Coded-field accuracy.** A human-coded gold set per coded field (sentiment, topic, concern, commentator type, emotive headline, entity resolution, attribute and polarity). Define agreement targets per field and per language, and who codes it. A human-coded sample of articles, as Carma analysts produce for reports, is the natural source.
- **Aggregate correctness.** Known-answer tests: seed a small corpus where every expected count, share and rank is known, and check the aggregates exactly. Check the drill-through invariant on every rollup.
- **Aggregate stability.** How far does a headline number move when the coder, vocabulary version or model changes? Report that sensitivity so a change is a decision, not a surprise.
- **Rollup reconciliation.** Rollups equal a recount from the child records, within a stated tolerance and lag.

### 12. Decisions to put to the user

Raise choices that need a human: precision versus recall at the margin, index size versus write speed, segmentation method for Chinese, whether extra extensions or an external engine are acceptable, how much staleness a search may tolerate. For the analytical layer, also: which analytical questions are in scope, how duplicates count, full population or sampled enrichment (cost versus coverage), what the sentiment scale means and its range, whether external series are in scope, the time zone rule, the minimum n before a rate is flagged, and which controlled vocabularies exist and who owns them. Use the protocol in the context file.

## Output

Write the spec with these sections:

1. **Summary and applicability**
2. **Search use cases** (ad hoc, standing and analytical: users, volume, latency, false-negative cost; the analytical questions named)
3. **Searchable document** (fields, roles, derived fields with confidence)
4. **Language analysis plan** (English, Arabic, Chinese, fallback; normalisation; language mismatch handling)
5. **Entities and quotes** (resolution, aliases, match confidence, quote records)
6. **Index strategy** (options, recommendation, environment checks)
7. **Bucketing and partitioning** (scheme, tiers, standing-query grouping)
8. **Analytical layer** (grains and child records per article, dimensions and measures with numerator and denominator, vocabularies and groupings, scope definition, how aggregates are served, drill-through invariant, honest-number rules, external series, time handling)
9. **Ranking and confidence presentation**
10. **Deduplication** (including how duplicates count in each measure)
11. **Freshness and coverage signalling** (including enrichment coverage)
12. **Recall, precision and aggregate evaluation plan**
13. **Risks and hot paths** (extend the architect FP/HP registers with `FP-S` and `HP-S` entries, same columns; include child-record write amplification and rollup maintenance)
14. **Handoff** (what carma-dba must implement, what carma-telemetry must measure, what carma-backend-testing must verify, what carma-ux must show)
15. **Decisions needed and open questions**

In the handoff, be specific for the analytical layer:
- carma-dba: child record tables and their rate per article, rollup tables and refresh, vocabulary and scope tables, external series tables, retention per grain.
- carma-telemetry: enrichment coverage per field, rollup lag, aggregate query latency, drill-through count mismatches.
- carma-backend-testing: known-answer aggregate tests, rollup reconciliation, coded-field accuracy against the gold set.
- carma-ux: show n, enrichment coverage, scope and comparison set next to every figure; drill-through from every bar and number; low-n flags.

## Persisting the work (when run inside a codebase)

Follow "Spec conventions" in the context file. Number with `python scripts/next_spec_number.py .specs/search`, write `.specs/search/NNNN-<feature-slug>.md` with `spec: carma-searchability` front matter and list the architect spec under `inputs`. Edit in place while `draft`. Do not write ADRs yourself: when the user decides a search-design question, tell them it should be recorded and suggest running carma-architect to codify it as an ADR in `.specs/architect/adrs/`.

If you are not in a codebase, deliver the output in the conversation and offer to save it.

## Appendix: analytical data points checklist

Use this to check that the design can answer typical Carma report questions. Examples are generic; replace them with the feature's own entities and vocabularies. In reports the coded fields are often produced by human analysts. In the PoC they are derived automatically, so each carries confidence and origin (P6, P7) and can be overridden by a person (P9).

### A. Grains: the units that get counted

One article can hold many mentions, quotes and references, so these are separate records linked to the article. A percentage is only meaningful when the grain of the numerator and the denominator is stated.

| Grain | Example measure | Why it is its own record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Article | Share of a market's coverage that mentions a theme | Base unit and the usual denominator. |
| Headline | Share of headlines that are emotive rather than factual | A property of the headline text; headline and body can disagree. |
| Entity mention | Articles mentioning a brand, with sentiment toward it | Many entities per article, each with its own sentiment. |
| Quote | Who was quoted, how negatively, about what | Each has a speaker, speaker type, polarity and topic. Many per article. |
| Attribute reference | Positive and negative references to a quality (such as competence) for one brand | Counts references, not articles; one article can hold several. |
| Topic or theme tag | Number of times a theme appeared | Multi-label per article. |
| Concern or issue tag | Share of articles with at least one concern | Multi-label; reported as "at least one". |
| Event annotation | A dated event that explains a peak | An annotation layer on the time axis, not an article attribute. |
| External observation | Search-interest index, survey wave result | Not article data; joined by market, time and term. |
| Scope | The saved definition of what a report covers | Makes a number reproducible. |

### B. Fields per grain

"Multi" means several values per record. "Derived" means produced by enrichment and carries confidence and origin.

- **Article and source:** market, outlet, outlet tier, language (stored and detected), `published_at` and its day, week and month buckets, article-level sentiment (derived; state what it is toward, its scale and its midpoint), in-scope flag, sample flag.
- **Headline:** emotive or factual (derived), entities named in the headline (multi).
- **Entity mention:** entity id, type, role, match confidence, per-entity sentiment (derived), time-varying attributes with validity dates, parent and subsidiary links, prominence (headline, lead, passing).

- **Tags:** theme and concern, from versioned vocabularies, with co-occurrence derivable.
- **External series and events:** value, market, term or question, date or wave, sample size, scale, source; event date, text, market or global.

3. **Ranks are relative to a stated set.** The same entity ranks differently among all entities and among a subset. Store the set and the tie handling.
4. **Aggregates drill through.** Every count can be turned into the records that produced it, and the list size equals the count (P8).
